subject: Capacity squeeze: proposal for shared-priority matrix (Bridgeway vs Nimbus)
snippet: Proposal for a deterministic priority matrix to avoid preemption between Bridgeway and Nimbus pilots.
messages:
From: Simon Lee <simon@bridgeway.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, sales@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@bridgeway.ai
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot capacity ask — Bridgeway preferring steady throughput for Q4 pilot

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Bridgeway is aiming to run a 6-week pilot starting 2026-12-01 for our conversational search feature. Two asks up front:

1) Can Redwood commit to a baseline of 32 GPU-hours/day for the pilot window (with headroom for short bursts)?
2) We have a planned ramp and cannot tolerate preemption that causes >200ms tail latency spikes for >5% of requests.

We understand you have competing Dedicated commitments in the same fleet (we heard Nimbus also signed a pilot). We need visibility into how you’ll prioritize and whether we can get a contract clause for guaranteed baseline capacity or an SLA carveout.

Attaching a short MA plan and expected traffic profile. Happy to jump on a call.

Best,
Simon Lee
Head of Product, Bridgeway
Bridgeway.ai

Attachments: Bridgeway_Pilot_MA_Plan_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Simon Lee <simon@bridgeway.ai>, procurement@bridgeway.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — Bridgeway preferring steady throughput for Q4 pilot

Simon —

Really appreciate the clear profile. Short answer: we can design for the baseline you describe, but we need to align on prioritization when capacity contention arises. We have two in-flight pilots (Bridgeway and Nimbus) with overlapping windows. To avoid reactive preemption calls, I propose we create a simple priority matrix that ties guarantees to committed spend, ramp profile, and latency SLOs.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal review with capacity ops (Ben + Monica) to map current reserved pools and realistic headroom.
- Share a one-page priority matrix with both parties (transparent) that codifies baseline guarantees vs burst arbitration rules.
- If Bridgeway needs contractual guarantees, route procurement/legal after we confirm pool reservations.

Ben/Monica — can you run a snapshot of dedicated pools for 11/30-12/31 (include pre-reserved slots, current surge capacity, and probable maintenance windows)? Please also flag any existing tranches that would block a hard commit. I attached their MA plan for context.

Simon — can you confirm whether Bridgeway is willing to convert pilot spend to a short reserve (30-day minimum) in exchange for priority? That would simplify the matrix.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Simon Lee <simon@bridgeway.ai>
Date: Sat, 14 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — Bridgeway preferring steady throughput for Q4 pilot

Ava/Monica —

Snapshot attached (capacity_snapshot_20261114.png). Quick summary:
- Fleet: 480 GPU-hours/day nominal across the cluster region Bridgeway targets.
- Reserved: 180 GPU-hours/day already reserved for Dedicated customers (including one large annual commit).
- Soft headroom: ~120 GPU-hours/day depending on batching/quantization choices.
- Maintenance & safety buffer: 40 GPU-hours/day typically withheld.

Immediate implication: we cannot grant both Bridgeway and Nimbus full hard baselines of 32 GPU-hours/day without either short-term burst capacity or moving one of them to a reserve commitment.

Suggestion: build a two-axis priority matrix where we score customers by: (A) committed baseline (reserve), (B) latency criticality, (C) strategic value (enterprise logo / upsell potential). Each dimension 0-3, higher score gets primary sloting during contention.

For Bridgeway specifically — if they commit to a 30-day reserve at 28 GPU-hours/day, we can map them to "Priority Tier A" which gives them entitlement to baseline plus defined burst credits (20% of baseline) before preemption. If no reserve, they fall to "Tier B" and are eligible for best-effort bursts only.

Laura — need legal input on whether we can propose a 30-day reserve as a contract clause for the pilot (short reserve addendum).

Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Capacity & Partnerships | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 08:38:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — Bridgeway preferring steady throughput for Q4 pilot

Thanks team —

Quick legal check: a short-form reserve addendum is fine for pilots, provided we: (1) limit indemnities tied to performance to the reserved baseline only, (2) state explicit burst arbitration rules, and (3) include a 72-hour notice window for any planned maintenance that would affect the baseline.

We should avoid hard SLA credits for pilot-level reserves (we can offer service credits for demonstrable outages above baseline but keep limits). I'll draft a 1-page addendum and loop in procurement counsel if Bridgeway wants their standard PO language included.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — Bridgeway preferring steady throughput for Q4 pilot

Simon —

Thanks for bearing with our internal triage. We ran the numbers and attached a proposed priority matrix (priority_matrix_proposal.pdf) that is intentionally simple:

- Tier A (Reserve commit >= 80% baseline): entitlement = baseline + 20% burst credits; 72-hour maintenance notice
- Tier B (No reserve / high latency need): entitlement = best-effort baseline; bursts are lowest-preempt priority
- Tier C (Ad-hoc/low commitment): best-effort, subject to preemption for Tier A/B needs

Concrete option for Bridgeway: convert pilot to a 30-day reserve at 28 GPU-hours/day. In return we’ll commit to Tier A entitlements for the pilot window and provide a simple addendum drafted by Laura. If Bridgeway declines a short reserve, we’ll still run the pilot but must label it Tier B and will not include contractual preemption protection.

If acceptable, I can schedule a triage call tomorrow with Ben/Monica to walk through the snapshot and sign the addendum after you confirm. Also copying Claire from Nimbus so both customers can see the transparent matrix — we believe transparency reduces surprise escalations.

Proposed triage call: Tue 2026-11-16 10:30am PT (30m). Confirm availability?

Thanks,
Ava
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
